advancement.kultivator.tempat.tema_air_a: Save the child who fell into the canal in heavy rain.
A Hand in the Rushing Water
advancement.kultivator.tempat.tema_air_b: Find Scholar Wen Shi's last couplet.
advancement.kultivator.tempat.tema_air_j: Collect your tailored silk robe from the House of Su Silk.
advancement.kultivator.tempat.tema_air_p: Drum the winning boat of the Dragon Boat Race.
advancement.kultivator.tempat.tema_air_t: Pick your first tea with Lu Yuqing.
Stop the Water Rats' black skiff.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_anak_je: The child who fell into the canal in the downpour is home safe. %s pulled the little one to the washing steps.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_bait_tu: Wen Shi's last couplet for his granddaughter is whole again; %s found it. It hangs in the Pavilion of Listening to Rain now.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_benang_: The House of Su is weaving day and night again. Madam Su says it is all thanks to %s, then refuses to say more.
%s released a red cloth on the lake. The House of Su's silkworms are eating again, thank heavens.
Last night a great red lantern sailed the lake, and the shadow of a bride waved from it. They say %s released it.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_harapan: %s released a lantern on Lantern Lake. Only the water knows the wish.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_juara_n: Did you hear? %s drummed the winning dragon boat. The beat was like a dragon's heart.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_lao_shu: Lao Shu the Old Rat sits in the water-gate jail. The canal thieves have lost their head.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_lentera: No moon tonight. Everyone is releasing lotus lanterns on the canals, are you coming?
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_perahu_: The drums are sounding at the boatyard! The Dragon Boat Race is starting, hurry to the bridges!
The boat whose drum %s beat won by one dragon's head. Its rowers have not stopped cheering.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_teh_per: %s picked the spring tea with Lu Yuqing. The tea master says those hands are light as dew.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_tikus: The Water Rats robbed again last night. Lock your stall chest, and do not sleep in the boat.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_tikus_t: %s caught a canal thief with bare hands! The water-market traders owe them.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_1: Sixty-four bridges, and outsiders always say a thousand. We never correct them.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_10: The lake fish at the Eating House is cooked with rice wine and ginger. Come hungry.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_11: The rainy season is back. The paper umbrellas of the Twin Bridges sell out before sunrise.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_12: Madam Su turned down three proposals for her daughter this month. Jin'er says she'd rather marry a loom.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_13: Lu Yuqing brews tea for herself every dusk, with two cups. Nobody knows who the second cup is for.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_14: Scholar Wen Shi writes poems on the bridge, then throws them into the water. He says the canal is the best reader.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_15: When the canal rises to the third step, the Water Gate is half closed. The rowers grumble, but the houses stay dry.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_16: The mulberry leaves from the western village are late again. The House of Su's silkworms are hungry and the weavers fret.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_17: The tea pickers say a cultivator meditates on the Tea Terraces every dawn. The leaves around him grow more fragrant.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_18: The water market cat can tell a fishing boat from a post boat. It only ever jumps onto the fishing boats.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_19: In the Zhang Residence hangs a painting of the Twin Bridges older than the bridges themselves. Think about that.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_2: The House of Su buys mulberry leaves from three villages. Their silkworms are fussier than capital officials.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_20: The morning mist on the lake is thick as silk. Auntie Chuan rows with her eyes shut and never hits a thing.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_3: This spring's Bi Luo is so fragrant the pickers on the terraces keep sneezing.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_4: Auntie Chuan once sang from the Water Gate to the Twin Bridges without drawing breath. So she says.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_5: On moonless nights, do not sit alone in the Moon-in-Water Pavilion.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_6: The Zhang Residence has six courtyards and, its servants say, seven ghosts. One for each courtyard, plus one who likes the kitchen.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_7: Painters from the capital came again to paint the Twin Bridges. They always draw the boats too small.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_8: When it rains, the scholars actually go out to the Pavilion of Listening to Rain. Strange people, scholars.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_air_umum_9: The Water Gate closes at nine at night. Anyone still outside must row the long way round the ring canal.
kultivator.cerita.quest.tema_air_anak_je: The boatmen pulled the child out before you arrived.
The boatmen pulled the child out with a pole. They are safe, only cold.
You carried the child to the washing steps. Their mother hugged you both, soaking wet, for a long time.
Heavy rain made the bridges slick, and a child fell into the canal.
Swim to the child, click them, then bring them to the nearest washing steps.
kultivator.cerita.quest.tema_air_bait_tu: Play Couplet Matching with Wen Shi and find the second line of the lost couplet.
Wen Shi copied the couplet with his finest brush and hung it in the Pavilion of Listening to Rain.
Recite the whole couplet to Wen Shi.
The second line of Wen Shi's last couplet for his granddaughter is lost among the Couplet Matching verses.
At night on Lantern Lake: calm three Canal Spirits by releasing a lotus lantern near them.
The cloth drifted to the middle of the lake and sank in silence. The canal runs clean again and the silkworms recovered, but no one knows whether Xiu Niang ever saw it.

Xiu Niang's Cloth sailed like a great lantern, and the weaver's spirit faded into light. The silkworms of the House of Su are eating again. Madam Su gave you the Red Thread Silk Robe and the title Night Weaver.
Weave Xiu Niang's Cloth with Su Jin'er at the red loom: 6 Cloud Silk, 10 Dew Tea Leaves, 1 Holy Water (the Water God's shrine basin blesses one bottle for you).
Tonight, keep watch near the Morning Water Market or the House of Su. Chase the Water Rats' black skiff and stop it with a blow.
Lao Shu is caught. Talk to him before he slinks away.
Tell Madam Su Jin what you found.
On the next Night of Water Lanterns (new-moon night), release Xiu Niang's Cloth at a lantern jetty on Lantern Lake.
Show the bottle of oily water to Lu Yuqing at the Cloud Tea Pavilion.
The Red Thread Beneath the Water
Take Auntie Chuan's canal tour at night (19:00 to 05:00) and watch the water near the Morning Water Market.
The silkworms of the House of Su are dying tray by tray. Madam Su Jin is sure something is wrong with the mulberry leaves or the canal water.
The cloth drifts away with no one waiting for it.
At night, go to the Moon-in-Water Pavilion on the garden pond. Xiu Niang waits there.
Xiu Niang goes home with the light.
Examine a mulberry leaf in the House of Su orchard (click the leaves) and fill a glass bottle from the canal in front of the house.
Scholar Wen Shi in the Scholar's Garden knows the tale of the lantern against the current. Go to him.
kultivator.cerita.quest.tema_air_perahu_: Your boat won the Dragon Boat Race. The boatyard still sings your beat.
Auntie Chuan's boat has lost its drummer. Win the Dragon Boat Race as a drummer.
On race day (every 14 days, at 14:00) sign up as a drummer at the Dragon Boat House and drum your boat to victory.
kultivator.cerita.quest.tema_air_teh_per: Bring your picked leaves to Lu Yuqing.
Lu Yuqing roasted the leaves you picked and gave you five Bi Luo Teas. You may brew for yourself at the Cloud Tea Pavilion: Bi Luo costs you a quarter less.
In spring from 04:00 to 08:00, pick 10 shoots from the tea bushes on the Tea Hill terraces.
Lu Yuqing wants you to pick tea with your own hands, just once, in spring.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_ahli_teh.mula: The first cup washes the leaves, the second is for the guest, the third is for friendship. Please.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_chuan_juara.m: Champions! The whole boatyard is still talking about it. Ah Bo says he refuses to heal, so you can stay our drummer. Wear that ribbon with pride.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_chuan_noda.mu: Madam Su sent you? Oily water... yes, I have smelled it a few nights now near the market. Let us look together. But only at night: by day a stain like that hides under the glitter of the sun.
Night has come. Take me on a night tour.
I will come back at night.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_chuan_noda.tu: Good. Bring three coins for the tour, Auntie Chuan has to eat too. And wear dark clothes: canal rats do not like being watched.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_chuan_sapa.la: The yuloh oar creaks softly, the stone bridge bows in silence; who leaves on the morning boat comes home by evening lantern. ...Ha! My voice was better once. Now only the fish applaud.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_chuan_sapa.ma: The Old Rat slips a letter under my oar every full moon. His hand is ugly and his spelling uglier, but the content is useful: which boats carry oil, who wears red robes. I read it, burn it, then pretend I never read it. He says he misses the smell of the canals.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_chuan_sapa.mu: Get in, get in! Auntie Chuan's boat never tips over, except once, and that was the duck's fault. Where to? The canals of this town are like threads on a loom: they all cross each other.
I want to hire a boat.
Take me on a canal tour.
Lanterns are sold only on the Night of Water Lanterns.
Tell me about the Dragon Boat Race.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_chuan_sapa.na: Every fourteen days we row two laps of Lantern Lake, four dragon boats, twenty oars each. The Red Boat has lacked a drummer since Ah Bo broke his arm. The drum gives the beat: on time and the boat flies; late and it stumbles. Will you take his place?
Come to the Dragon Boat House at the boatyard on race day, at two in the afternoon, and click the boat you want to drum for. Then follow the beat.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_chuan_sapa.pe: Lao Shu carves little boats out of fish bones in his cell at the Water Gate prison. The guards sell them to children, two coppers each. He says it is the first honest money he ever made. He does not like the taste of it.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_jiner_kain.ca: Bring six Cloud Silk, ten Dew Tea Leaves and one Holy Water, then click the red loom in the weaving hall. Follow my rhythm. If your thread tangles we repeat the pass; nothing is used up until the cloth is done.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_jiner_kain.mu: Mother says we will finish Xiu Niang's cloth? At last! I learned the pattern by heart from the half that remains: a red river flowing into the moon. Three passes: the ground, the river, then the moon.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_jiner_lepas.m: The cloth is so beautiful I almost cannot let it go. But it is not ours. On the next Night of Water Lanterns take it to a lantern jetty on the lake and release it like a lantern. Let the water carry it home.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_jiner_sapa.di: Never again. I sit there every new-moon night and wait for the pedal to move. Sometimes I think the thread trembles, sometimes I think it is only the wind off the canal. Perhaps she is still angry that we drove her away.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_jiner_sapa.me: That is Xiu Niang's loom. Nobody may sit there, they say it brings bad luck. I sat there once as a child. The pedals moved before my feet touched them. I was not afraid. It felt like someone wanted to teach me.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_jiner_sapa.mo: A red river flowing into the moon. Xiu Niang's pattern. Buyers from the capital ask for it by that name now, and Mother pretends to be annoyed that the price went up. I weave one gold thread into every cloth, where no one can see it. That one is for her.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_jiner_sapa.mu: Shh, do not tell Mother I am taking a break. Want to learn weaving? The rhythm is like rowing: pull, tread, throw, beat. If the thread sings, you are doing it right.
Tell me about that red loom.
Does the red loom still move on its own?
Does the red loom still move on its own?
What are the weavers talking about?
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_jiner_sapa.pa: Just once more, the night after the cloth sailed. The pedal went down slowly, one time, like someone nodding before leaving. It has been still ever since. I cried a little. Do not tell Mother.
Shh! Don't stand so close, people will know we are acquainted. News from the drains: the black skiffs sail toward the mountains now, not the sea. Someone moved the route.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_lao_shu_tangk: A man in a red robe. Never lowers his hood, hands cold as dead fish. Says he is from the Demon City, the town that is not on decent people's maps. The oil is for 'guests' there. I am only a rat! A rat does not ask the cat where it goes.
I am handing you to the guards.
Go. But from now on you are my spy.
A spy? Me? Ha... fine, fine. If the red robe comes again, you will be the first to know. This old rat has ears in every drain.

Mercy, mercy! This old rat only carries crates, I swear! I don't know what's in them! ...All right, I know the smell. Shadow Oil. Handed from a ship down to my skiff every new moon, paid in silver that is too heavy.
The water-gate jail is cold and wet! ...Well, at least there are no men in red robes there.
Napkins from the House of Su? Dry, folded, unopened. Madam Su chose a good courier. Give her my thanks, and tell her this season's tea is too fragrant for ordinary napkins.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_lu_minyak.mul: A black stain that reflects no lantern light? Show me your bottle. ...Yes. Shadow Oil. Pressed from the roots of trees that grow on demonic soil. Smugglers coat their crates with it so the water-gate dogs cannot smell them.
You know a lot for a tea master.
The same smuggling happens in the harbour towns.
The same smuggling put out the beacon in the harbour towns.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_lu_minyak.pel: So you have seen it there too. Then this is not one canal gang's doing. Someone opened a route from the sea to our canals, and that route begins somewhere far darker than any harbour.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_lu_minyak.rah: Tea and secrets are both kept in sealed jars. My guests are merchants, officials, sometimes smugglers who wish to look respectable. They talk over the second cup. I only pour.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_lu_minyak.tik: The Water Rats. Canal thieves led by Lao Shu the Old Rat: they rob the stall boats at night and flee in a black skiff. If anyone carries that oil on our canals, it is them. Keep watch tonight near the Morning Water Market or the House of Su. Rats always return to the same granary.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_lu_sapa.cawan: My master, Lord Lu Mingyuan, picked me up from the washing steps when I was a baby and gave me his name. Fifty years ago he waited at his house in wedding clothes for a boat that never arrived. He never married. Before he died he asked me to pour a second cup every dusk, for someone still on her way.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_lu_sapa.koson: On the night the cloth sailed I poured the second cup as always. In the morning it was empty, and there were no ants, no cat, no wind. I still pour it. But now I pour for two people who finally met.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_lu_sapa.masih: The tea in the second cup is always cold by morning, and still full. I will keep pouring it. My master waited fifty years; I can wait a little longer.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_lu_sapa.mulai: Sit. Water for tea must not boil wildly, only like crab eyes: small bubbles rising slowly. The same is true of conversation.
What tea grows on the northern hill?
I brought fresh tea leaves to sell.
Could you teach me to pick tea?
Who is the second cup you pour every dusk for?
What do people talk about in the pavilion?
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_lu_sapa.petik: Tea you pick with your own hands tastes different. Not better. More honest. Come to the tea terraces in spring, at dawn, from four to eight in the morning. Pick ten shoots from the tea azaleas: only the bud and the two leaves below it. Then bring them here.
I will come back with the leaves.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_lu_sapa.teh: Bi Luo, the 'green snail', because the leaf curls like a snail shell and its scent startles people. Picked in spring before the dew dries. For one who meditates, a cup of Bi Luo makes the mind as clear as a windless lake.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_lu_teh_selesa: Look: you picked two shoots too long, and one leaf is bruised by your nail. No matter. I roasted them for you. From today you may brew for yourself at the pavilion tables: Bi Luo costs you a quarter less. Honest tea for honest hands.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_pemelihara.mu: Hear that? That is the sound of silkworms eating mulberry leaves, like a little rain. Four times a day they eat, and four times a day I climb these racks. The silk you wear starts here.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_pemelihara_sa: Another tray this morning. The worms just lie still, they will not eat. I picked the leaves myself, fresh! I do not understand. Madam Su has not slept for three nights.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_pemetik.mulai: A bud and two leaves, no more. Greedy hands make bitter tea. In spring, before the dew dries, the whole hill smells sweet all the way down to the canal.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_pendayung.mul: Hey, mind your head under the bridge! The Post Boat comes every six minutes, just one coin. Board at any stop, get off at any stop.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_penenun.mulai: Sorry, my hands must not stop: if the warp slackens, a whole day's work is lost. Did you know, the crane pattern takes eleven thousand throws of the shuttle.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_sastrawan.mul: Hush. I almost found a rhyme for 'mist'. ...Gone again. You know, in this town even the boatmen can make verses. Scholars like us must work twice as hard.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_su_jin_bingki: From the Guild Board? Right on time. This parcel holds silk napkins for the Cloud Tea Pavilion: Lu Yuqing will not pour tea over any other cloth. Do not get it wet, and do not open it.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_su_jin_kain.b: It can, if the thread is right. Six rolls of Cloud Silk for the body. Ten Dew Tea Leaves from the tea terraces for the river-green dye. And one bottle of Holy Water to steep the red thread: usually from the shrine in the oasis towns, but the basin of the Water God's shrine by our lake is blessed too, once for every sincere soul. Bring it all to Jin'er.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_su_jin_kain.j: Because my daughter weaves like Xiu Niang: too fast, too bold, and never listening to her mother. That red loom only moves for hands like hers.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_su_jin_kain.m: Wen Shi told me everything. Xiu Niang... her bridal cloth is still rolled in the chest above the red loom. Half of it. My mother kept it because she could not bring herself to burn it.
Auntie Chuan. She has rowed these canals since before I was born and sings under every bridge. She hires out boats at the Boatyard. Ask her for a night tour: if there is a stain on our water, her eyes will see it first.

The leaves are clean, the water oily... and it smells like a cheap oil lamp. No house upstream dumps oil into the canal: the Water Gate Warden's fines are too steep. Someone does it in secret, at night.
Who knows the canals at night?
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_su_jin_sapa.d: Cloud Silk fetches the best price in the capital and the desert towns; here it is cheapest, because we weave it. A clever trader buys here and sells far away. Your Trade Book will tell you the rest.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_su_jin_sapa.k: People call it the town of a thousand bridges. Count them yourself if you are patient: sixty-four. Every house has a front door to the street and a back door to the water. Our wealth comes from two things: silk, and tea from the northern hill.
I heard there is a legend about a weaver.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_su_jin_sapa.l: Xiu Niang. The finest weaver who ever sat at this house's looms, fifty years ago. She drowned on her wedding night and her bridal cloth was never finished. My mother said that on moonless nights one lantern sails against the current. I do not believe ghost stories. But I never sold that red loom either.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_su_jin_sapa.m: Welcome to the House of Su Silk. Mind your sleeves: thread here costs more than silver.
How long has this house been weaving?
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_su_jin_sapa.u: Five generations. My great-grandmother kept silkworms in bamboo trays in the attic; I write letters to merchants of three harbour towns. Only one thing never changed: a broken thread is never knotted in secret.
And where does the silk go?
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_su_jin_terima: I saw that red light from the attic window, sailing to the middle of the lake and rising like incense smoke. I do not believe ghost stories. I believe in promises woven to the end. That night the two happened to be the same.
She weaves the red river pattern into every cloth now, and buyers from the capital ask for it by name. Do not tell her I am proud. She would listen to her mother even less.

I moved it to the front hall, where every buyer can see it. Nobody weaves on it except Jin'er, once a year, on the new-moon night. She says the thread no longer pulls her hand. Now she pulls the thread.
My silkworms are eating again. Do you hear it? Like fine rain on the roof tiles. This house is in your debt, Night Weaver: your price here will always be lighter.
Do you believe in ghost stories now?
Did Xiu Niang ever see her cloth?

No one knows. The cloth sank without a sound. My silkworms recovered, the water is clean, and I am grateful. But every new-moon night I light one lantern on the jetty, in case she is still looking for the way home.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_su_jin_ulat.b: An ordinary sickness kills one tray, not twenty. And an ordinary sickness does not blacken leaves picked this very morning before noon. Something is wrong with the leaves, or with the water.
Fine, I will look into it.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_su_jin_ulat.m: You are from outside, are you not? Good. The townsfolk already talk too much. My silkworms are sick: they stop eating, their bodies go pale, the leaves in the trays blacken from the edges. Half the trays died in three days.
I will find out what causes it.
Maybe it is just an ordinary silkworm sickness?
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_su_jin_ulat.t: Examine the mulberry leaves in the orchard behind this house: click the leaves on a tree. Then fill a bottle from the canal in front of our water door. The silkworm keepers wash the trays with that water every morning.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_wen_bait_sele: 'The red thread beneath the water waits for the hand that ties it.' Yes... that is it. Fifty years I searched for that line, and a stranger found it in one afternoon. Perhaps poems simply prefer strangers.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_wen_kisah.cuc: My granddaughter, my daughter's child. She wove at the House of Su from the age of nine. On her wedding night the skiff carrying her to the groom's house struck a dark bridge pier: someone had stolen the stern lantern that night. She drowned in the wedding gown she wove herself. Her cloth is still half done.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_wen_kisah.len: Yes. These canals always had rats. For fifty years I wrote sad poems about it, and not one made the water any brighter. If restless spirits rise from the lake, it is because something woke them: foul water keeps the dead from sleeping.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_wen_kisah.mul: You ask about the lantern that sails against the current. Sit. I am one hundred and twelve years old; the thin cultivation I learned when young did not make me strong, it only made me live too long and remember too much.
Who was Xiu Niang to you?
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_wen_kisah.ten: Take these three lotus lanterns; I made them myself from my worst poems. At night go to Lantern Lake. When the canal spirits rise, release a lantern near them. Light reminds them of the way home. Then meet her at the Moon-in-Water Pavilion. She always waits there.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_wen_sapa.bait: The last couplet I wrote for my granddaughter is lost. I remember its first line, not its second. I slipped it among the Couplet Matching verses so the garden wind could not steal it, and then forgot which one. Would you look for it, for an old man?
Play Couplet Matching with me. The lost couplet will come up first. Pick the second line that makes your heart ache the right way.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_wen_sapa.batu: Lake rocks. Water wore at them for a thousand years until only their will remained. A scholar chooses rocks as he chooses friends: the ones with the most holes, because the wind can pass through and sing.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_wen_sapa.bula: Through the moon gate the view beyond becomes a painting in a round frame. The old folk say whoever walks through with their beloved on a full-moon night will meet again in the next life. I have walked through a hundred times. Alone.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_wen_sapa.cucu: I watched from the Pavilion of Listening to Rain. She waved, young one. My stubborn granddaughter waved to me the way she did at nine, leaving to weave for the first time. I wrote a new couplet that night. The first in fifty years that is not sad.
The canal water is clear again; that is more than an old man may ask. But my garden is too quiet now. On new-moon nights I used to hear a loom in the distance. Now only frogs.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_wen_sapa.mula: Rain on the banana leaves, frogs in the winding pond. This garden was made for listening, not for looking. Sit, young one, and do not step on the moss.
Why are those rocks full of holes?
Tell me about the moon gate.
Did you see the red lantern, grandfather?
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_xiu_temui.den: My cloth. A red river flowing into the moon. I promised my bridegroom he would see that river finished on our wedding night. I cannot leave before that promise is woven. The thread still waits for me at the red loom.
I will finish it for you.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_xiu_temui.jan: You... truly? Then release the cloth to the water on a moonless night, like a lantern. I will wait on the lake. I will wait, as I did before.
kultivator.cerita.tema_air_xiu_temui.mul: The stern lantern... someone stole it that night. The water under the bridge was so cold. My gown was heavy. I cried for grandfather, but only the frogs answered. Who are you? Why do you not run like the others?
I am here to listen. Tell me.
This spirit does not trust you yet (Nama Baik 20 in this town).
Begone, spirit! Back to the water!
kultivator.kota_tema.air.anak.bawa: Bring the child to the nearest washing steps.
kultivator.kota_tema.air.anak.jatuh: A child slipped off a slick bridge into the rushing canal! Swim over, click them, then bring them to the washing steps.

kultivator.kota_tema.air.tur.tempat.derm: This is the Boatyard. In that shed the boats lie upside down on trestles waiting to be caulked. Two dragon boats sleep in their own house: their dragon heads are carved from a single camphor trunk.
The boatyard! My first kiss was here, behind boat number three.
kultivator.kota_tema.air.tur.tempat.jemb: The Twin Bridges. One round-arched, one square-arched, meeting at the corner of two canals like a key and its lock. A painter from the capital drew them and called it Memory of the Hometown.
The Twin Bridges, look at the arches!
kultivator.kota_tema.air.tur.tempat.pang: The Water Stage in the middle of Lantern Lake. On the Night of Water Lanterns a singer stands there and the whole town releases lotus lanterns. The little pagoda on the island is for the Water God; his shrine is on the shore, and its basin is blessed.
The Water Stage. On the next new moon, you must see it!
kultivator.kota_tema.air.tur.tempat.pasa: The Morning Water Market. Before sunrise the boats moor and become stalls: lake fish, tofu, rice cakes, paper umbrellas. At night this place is quiet, too quiet for my taste.
The water market! So busy here in the mornings.
kultivator.kota_tema.air.tur.tempat.pint: The Water Gate. Its wooden leaf comes down at nine every night and rises at five in the morning. The clerks in the tower check every crate that comes in: smugglers fear their dogs.
The Water Gate! Don't get locked outside.
kultivator.kota_tema.air.tur.tempat.ruma: The House of Su Silk, five generations. In the first courtyard silkworms eat mulberry leaves on tiered racks; in the weaving hall six looms sing all day. The red one at the end is never used. Don't ask why. Well, ask.
The House of Su. Hear the looms?
kultivator.kota_tema.air.tur.tempat.tama: The Scholar's Garden. Behind that white wall lie a winding pond, hollow rock hills and two pavilions. Scholar Wen Shi keeps it. He is very old, older than our youngest bridge.
The scholar's garden. Hush a little, don't disturb his poems.
kultivator.kota_tema.air.xiu.lentera: A lantern sails against the current toward the Moon-in-Water Pavilion. On its floor stands a girl in a soaking wedding dress.
kultivator.kota_tema.air.xiu.muncul: You can see me...? No one has turned to look in fifty years.
